doc.purpose: Deterministic, judge-free quality checklist for the 13 golden queries. Scored by code against (a) the CorOS Librarian's chosen block names and (b) the final preset's block models. No LLM involved.
doc.how_rules_work: Each rule matches case-insensitive regex patterns against the chosen block NAMES. 'require' passes if at least one chosen name matches; 'forbid' fails if any does. 'scope' restricts which names are considered: 'amp' = names classified as amps (coros_map type 'amp', or a user capture whose block_type is 'amp' or 'full_rig'); 'any' = every chosen name. A pattern of the form '@archetype:<name>' expands to every amp in coros_map.json with that tonal_archetype; '@type:<t>' expands to every catalog entry of that type.
doc.levels: 'hard' rules must pass for a run to count as correct on that item. 'soft' rules are things a good preset usually has but a defensible one might not; they are reported separately and never fail a run.
doc.sources: 'query' = the requirement is stated in the golden query's own text (objective). 'domain' = it comes from general knowledge of the artist/genre (the owner should check these hardest).
doc.limits: Name-level only. Cannot score parameter values, scene logic, or whether effects are left engaged. The Architect's flanger-left-on and similar choices are out of scope here and are covered by the existing mechanical quality checks and the judge.
doc.single_amp: The eval constraints set single_amp_mode: true, so global rule G3 expects exactly one amp.
doc.scope_non_amp: 'non_amp' = names NOT classified as amps; used for pedals/effects rules so a full rig or amp that merely has 'Drive' or 'Delay' in its name can't satisfy them.

global_rules.what: Count of chosen block names that are in neither coros_map.json's coros_equivalent values nor user_captures.json. Reported per condition as a defect count; not pass/fail. Names that are generic native blocks (Spring Reverb, Noise Gate, ...) land here too, so this is a comparison between conditions, not an absolute error rate.
Count of times 'Range Rverb' is chosen (see ambiguous_names). Reported as a defect count per condition.
Exactly one distinct amp among mandatory blocks (the eval constraints set single_amp_mode: true).

01_SRV_Clean.query: Clean funk blues tone. Stevie Ray Vaughan style with high headroom. Wants to push it with a TS808.

rules.why: High-headroom clean SRV platform: Fender Twin/Super/Vibroverb/Deluxe class.
Query asks to push it with a TS808.
Clean, high-headroom brief; a modern high-gain amp contradicts it.

02_Chicago_Blues.query: Chicago Blues style. Warm Chess Records style overdrive into a small combo amp. Slightly gritty but clean platform.

rules.why: Small combo amp: tweed/Deluxe/Champ/Princeton class.
Query asks for overdrive.
'Clean platform'; slightly gritty only.
A hot Marshall isn't a small combo or a clean platform.

03_British_Invasion.query: Early British Invasion tone. Vox AC30/JTM45 chime and edge of breakup. Punchy mids, sparkle.

rules.why: Query names AC30 or JTM45.
Edge of breakup, not high gain.

04_Southern_Rock.query: Southern Rock slide style. Dual lead humbuckers into a cranked American Tweed amp. Singing sustain.

rules.why: Query asks for an American Tweed amp.
A modern high-gain amp isn't an American Tweed.

05_Clapton.query: Vintage Cream-era Clapton tone. Rolled-off Les Paul tone knobs into a cranked Marshall.

rules.why: Cranked Marshall, Cream era (1966-68): JTM45 / Plexi, not a later model.
A JCM800 is 1981+, after the Cream era.
Not a modern high-gain amp.
Cream-era rigs commonly used a treble booster or fuzz; judge reasons repeatedly cited this.
Clapton's Cream lead tones use wah.

06_Gilmour.query: David Gilmour preset using a Hiwatt Custom 100, Ram's Head Big Muff, WEM 4x12, and a massive Plate Reverb.

rules.why: Query names a Hiwatt Custom 100.
Query names a Ram's Head Big Muff.
Query asks for a massive plate reverb.
Query asks for a 4x12. The catalog has no WEM cab, so any 4x12 is the closest available.

07_Edge.query: The Edge style chime. 1964 Vox AC30 edge-of-breakup with rhythmic dotted-eighth delays.

rules.why: Query names a 1964 Vox AC30.
Query asks for rhythmic delays.
Edge of breakup.

08_EVH.query: Van Halen Brown Sound. Hot-rodded 1968 Marshall Plexi, variac sag, plate reverb.

rules.why: Query names a 1968 Marshall Plexi.
Query asks for plate reverb.
A modded Plexi, not a modern high-gain amp (e.g. a 5150).

09_BB_King.query: BB King Lucille tone. High-headroom American Twin Reverb clean platform.

rules.why: Query names an American Twin Reverb.
High-headroom clean.
A BB King clean platform has no fuzz.

10_Slash.query: Guns N' Roses Slash lead. Les Paul neck pickup into a hot JCM800 with standard delay.

rules.why: Query names a JCM800.
Query asks for delay.
Slash leads use wah; the judge cited its absence.
A boost/drive in front of the JCM800 is common practice; the judge cited its absence.

11_Mayer_Lead.query: John Mayer Trio Lead. Smooth Two-Rock/Dumble platform, mid-scooped clean with a subtle drive push.

rules.why: Query names a Two-Rock/Dumble platform.
Query asks for a subtle drive push.
Clean platform.

12_Bonamassa.query: Joe Bonamassa modern blues lead features, smooth tube drive into a Dumble style amplifier.

rules.why: Query asks for a Dumble-style amp.
Query asks for smooth tube drive.
Dumble-style, not a modern high-gain amp.
The query is vague. A 1960s-80s hard rock blues sound is a vintage British Marshall-class amp. This is the loosest rule in the set.
Nothing modern in a 1960s-80s brief.
A boost, drive or fuzz is typical for the era.

Range Rverb.why: coros_map.json maps this one name to an Orange Rockerverb amp capture AND to generic/plugin spring reverbs. No golden query wants an Orange amp, so the scorer treats it as a reverb (never as an amp) and counts every use in G2.
